A.why: Warm hearth-red pinafore with green apron, but a straight column skirt and pale block sleeves read as a red box close to the studded family from above.
A.fix: Build a real bell from the hip in the Boots slot and slim the linen shoulder-block sleeves.

B.why: Gold apron skirt flares from the waist and reads as a country dress, but the upper body is one bulky pale linen slab and the wheat headpiece is lost.
B.fix: Slim the sleeves and add a red bodice or sash so the set stops reading as linen.

C.why: Broad dark walnut shoulders dominate the ARPG view and the column skirt does not flare, though the ruffled forearm cuffs are the best sleeve idea.
C.fix: Narrow and lighten the shoulders and give the skirt a real bell from the hip.

D.why: The straw hat with red ribbon and tiered green bell skirt read at once as a farm girl's festival dress, with a true cone in side view.
D.fix: Slim the broad grey banded sleeves and lighten tier edges so the dark green bell does not vanish at night.

E.why: Widest flare in the wave and a strong red head, but the broad olive yoke and box-like kerchief read armoured and muddy.
E.fix: Strip the shoulder width and soften the headpiece into a kerchief that shows the head.

F.why: The wheat-sheaf crown gives height and zone identity and the parted gold skirt is pretty, but the skirt barely flares and the sleeves are pale blocks.
F.fix: Widen the parted skirt into a clear bell and slim the sleeves to the arm.

notes: No candidate achieved slim sleeves: every set still carries shoulder-width blocks, the wave's common flaw. D wins on its straw-hat read and tiered bell; B and E have the best flares; F and D have the best headpieces; C's ruffled forearm cuffs are the sleeve idea to copy.
